standard_prerequisites.name: Dedekind cut
standard_prerequisites.statement: A Dedekind cut (L,U) of rationals is a pair of predicates with the usual roundedness and disjointness conditions; RD is the type of such cuts.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is the object of the statement and of the completion discussed in the proof.

standard_prerequisites.name: Dedekind completion and admissibility
standard_prerequisites.statement: The Dedekind completion of an ordered field is admissible for Omega when its cuts are again representable.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is the content of the retained context lemma used at source line 658.

standard_prerequisites.name: Finality of the Dedekind reals
standard_prerequisites.statement: Every archimedean ordered field admissible for Omega embeds into RD.
standard_prerequisites.use: It produces the two embeddings at source lines 659-660.

core_obligations: Quote the retained admissibility lemma to conclude that the Dedekind completion of RD is admissible for Omega (source line 658).
Apply the retained finality theorem to obtain embeddings of the completion into RD and of RD into the completion (source lines 659-660).
Show that these embeddings are isomorphisms because their composites are order-preserving field homomorphisms fixing the dense subfield of rationals, hence the identity (source lines 660-662).
Conclude Dedekind completeness from the fact that the embedding of the completion into RD is an isomorphism (source lines 662-663).

proof_roadmap.step: Admissibility of the completion and the two embeddings.
Identify the composites with the identity and conclude.

difficulty_reason: Counted unit is Corollary 11.2.16 at source lines 648-655: the Dedekind reals are Dedekind complete, i.e. every real-valued Dedekind cut has a unique real with the prescribed lower and upper classes. The author's proof (source lines 657-664) is a three-step argument that cannot be shortened: it first invokes the retained admissibility lemma for the Dedekind completion (line 658), then applies the retained finality theorem to get embeddings in both directions (lines 659-660), and then has to show that these embeddings are inverse to each other by the rigidity argument that an order-preserving field homomorphism fixing the dense rational subfield is the identity (lines 660-662) before the completeness statement follows (line 663). The statement records only the completeness property; the two labelled inputs and the rigidity step are invisible in it.
